messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Q4 Runway & GPU Efficiency — Leadership Prep

Team —

I pulled together the attached runway model and the latest batching experiments summary ahead of Friday's leadership sync. High-level asks:

- Quick sanity check on the assumptions (lines highlighted in yellow in runway_modeling_v2.xlsx). Notable ones: 12% QoQ product traffic growth, 60% steady-state GPU utilization target, and the proposed caching assumptions (see sheet 'cache_assumptions').
- Confirm whether we can/should push for a M2 capacity reserve (3x burst) for the first 6 weeks of Q4 to cover the holiday spike; CloudOps included on this thread for feasibility/timing.
- Decide on a single metric to present to the board: I recommend 'cost per successful request at p95 latency' (combines unit cost and SLO).

Attachments: runway_modeling_v2.xlsx, batching-experiments-summary.pdf (summary of the August experiments; includes per-model batching curves + tail-latency impacts).

Proposed outcomes for the Friday QBR prep: runway baseline, top-2 levers to gain 20% unit-cost reduction, and a one-slide risk mitigation plan if utilization drops below 50%.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole

Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Marissa —

THANKS for the package. Quick notes from a leadership angle:

- I agree on p95 cost-per-success as the headline metric. Clear, actionable.
- If M2 reserve is gated behind a cost commitment, we need a short justification slide that ties reserve cost to avoided SLA-penalty risk and revenue-at-risk for high-value customers (Acme included here).
- Let's keep the risk slide simple: 1) capacity (burst), 2) quality regressions (model swaps), 3) procurement lead times.

I'll be on Friday's prep and want the final runway table by Thursday EOD.

-Lauren

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Q4 Runway & GPU Efficiency — Leadership Prep

Marissa — good pack. Numbers we should call out for leadership:

- Current committed monthly GPU spend (prod fleet): $1.8M.
- Effective unit cost today (tokens + infra) for our top RLHF model at p95: $0.0019 per request; with caching + batching tuned in the August experiments we can hit $0.0015 at similar latency for the same traffic shape (best-case).
- Utilization: fleet wide 55% now; targeted steady state 60% is realistic but only if we implement prefix caching aggressively and re-run the scheduler to bias longer-lived sessions to warm hosts.

Two quick asks: 1) Marissa — include a sensitivity table that shows the runway delta for utilization bands 45/55/65%; 2) Karthik — we need a crisp note on how KV cache TTLs interact with multi-tenant eviction (one slide).

Vivek
Head of Serving Runtime

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 09:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Q4 Runway & GPU Efficiency — Leadership Prep

Folks —

Short technical summary for the slide deck (can be one bullet each):

- Batching: August experiments show diminishing returns past batch size ~64 for small prompt distributions; large prompts still benefit up to 128. Larger batches reduce per-token kernel overhead but push p95 up ~10-30ms depending on model and sequence length.
- Prefix/KV caching: prefix hits reduce total decode work by ~28% for chat patterns we see (typical 30% prefix reuse). TTL of 6h yields best tradeoff for warm sessions; but multi-tenant eviction policy needs to prioritize enterprise customers (can be configured by namespace weight).
- Quantization/compiled kernels: switching to the new int8 path in non-critical models reduces memory pressure and enables higher consolidation; expect ~12% lower GPU cost for those workloads, but need a validation guardrail for quality drift (we run evals on the rollout).

I will attach a one-slide tech note for the QBR. If leadership wants a short decision ask: authorize a controlled roll of int8 on 25% of non-production traffic and a one-week prefetched cache pilot for Acme Media.

-Karthik
SVP, Model Serving

Marissa / Team —

CloudOps can provision a 3x burst reservation starting 2026-11-20 with a 14-day lead (order submitted by 2026-11-06). Pricing: additional reserved capacity priced at a 9% premium vs spot-equivalent usage; or full-month dedicated nodes at 18% premium.

We recommend the 3x burst model (short-term reserve) for holiday windows — it gives fast scale with limited committed spend. To action we need a PO (or internal sign-off) by 2026-11-04.
